Jamie — thanks for the inventory and clear ask. I've looped in Marissa (storage/ops) and Kim (deploy scheduling). High level answers below; I'll follow up with a short design note and a proposed node-class PDF.

1) Node pool segmentation (recommended):
   - control-plane: 3 dedicated masters (taint: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule) on CPU-only hosts, 16GB RAM, 4 vCPU; etcd quorum on these nodes.
   - runtime-gpu: GPU-heavy node pool for inference; recommend 2 node classes: runtime-gpu-large (A100/80GB or equivalent) and runtime-gpu-small (A10/NVIDIA T4 class) to allow cost/latency routing.
   - storage-cache: SSD-only nodes (high IOPS NVMe) used for KV cache and temp stores; use local PVs with replication (see PVC notes below).
   - infra-services: small CPU nodes for logging/monitoring, ingress, and sidecar services.

2) PVC strategy:
   - Model artifacts: use a single shared NFS-backed ReadOnlyMany (ROX) class for model binaries — keep model store mounted read-only in runtime pods. Back this with a replicated NAS appliance or S3-compatible object store if you have one.
   - KV cache / KV-accelerator: for LM KV-cache, prefer local NVMe as ephemeral volumes (emptyDir with persistent volume-backed caching is fine) — recommended to use a StatefulSet with local persistent volumes and replication across nodes. Configure automatic eviction and TTL at the application level.
   - PVC sizes: set conservative defaults (20–100GB) for model caches, larger for model-store depending on model footprint.

3) IOPS/SLA:
   - For latency-critical inference (A100 class), target sustained 1000–2000 IOPS per node for small token sizes; plan NVMe with 1–3ms p99 latency.
   - For model artifact reads, NFS throughput of 400–600MB/s aggregate recommended during cold-model loading.

4) Network / firewall:
   - Outbound: installer needs egress to redwood-update.redwood.com (443) and telemetry endpoints.
   - Control plane ports: kube-apiserver (6443) open within VPC; we recommend restricting API server access to management jump hosts and the Redwood Private control plane.
   - Cross-node MTU: ensure jumbo frames disabled by default; we test on 1500 MTU.

Action items:
- Marissa: can you attach the PV & CSI configuration snippet and the proposed node-class PDF?
- Kim: please propose two 90-minute windows for Oct 23–25.

Sofia Ivanova
Manager, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

PV/CSI recommendations (summary):
- Use a dual-class storage approach: fast-local-nvme (StorageClass: fast-local-nvme, volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer, reclaimPolicy: Delete) for KV cache; csi driver: local-volume-provisioner with topology-aware binding.
- Shared model store: nfs-ha (StorageClass: nfs-ha, mountOptions: [ro], reclaimPolicy: Retain) — mount RO for runtime. Provide a cronjob to sync new model versions into the model store during off-peak windows to avoid cold-start thundering herd.
- Snapshot + Restore: recommend an hourly snapshot for KV cache metadata and daily snapshot for model-store index metadata. Use longhorn or your preferred CSI snapshotter integrated with your backup target.

Security note: ensure that the NFS export is restricted to the k8s CIDR and that the CSI driver runs with least privilege. We'll provide a PSG (privilege security guide) snippet for your security team.

Attachments: proposed-node-classes.pdf, redwood-onprem-checklist.md

—Marissa
